cards.title: git push
cards.body: `git push` uploads your commits to the remote. The first time, `git push -u origin main` also remembers where `main` goes.

cards.title: Next time, just push
cards.body: After that first `-u`, `git status` tells you when you are ahead of GitHub, and a plain `git push` sends your new commits.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: The push fails: Git cannot find a remote called `main`. Tap the bug.
cards.code:
git add .
git commit -m "Add about page"
git push -u main origin

bug.fix: The remote comes first, then the branch: `git push -u origin main`.

check.question: After `git push -u origin main` once, what can you type next time?
check.explanation: `-u` saved `origin main` as the upstream, so `git push` knows where to go.

exercise.prompt: Your repo is connected to GitHub as `origin`. Push `main` and set its upstream.
